overall.summary: All 173 claims and every drafted number reproduce; nothing is refuted. Seven weakenings: the root is said not to add up although it adds exactly in log-odds; the many-calls gate hypothesis omits its West Virginia exception; the calls-vs-evening-charge part names South Dakota as its partner and never mentions evening charge, the stronger one; two '1% to 1%' sentences; 'ignores' for linked inputs; 'patients' for customers.

findings.statement: It is made of those five parts plus the state and total international charge entering directly, combined in a way that does not simply add up.
findings.check: ablate --node 252 --to zero; probe sweep of day minutes, summing part contributions
findings.evidence: In log-odds the five parts add exactly: the implied constant is -4.86 at 90, 170 and 350 day minutes (within display rounding); the only non-additive unit, 252, changes no training prediction (max change 0.0000, AUC 0.9009 both ways). The non-additivity is only the final sigmoid. The sentence contradicts the root hypothesis and lead ('the model adds five parts').

uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-e8679c --hold typical --sweep 'total day minutes=90:350:14'

findings.statement: This gate does nothing until about 4 calls to customer service, then raises the predicted chance ... steadily.
findings.check: probe calls 0..9 for West Virginia and Idaho (typical customer)
findings.evidence: Idaho: gate 0 up to 3 calls, +0.59 logit at 4, +1.20 at 5. West Virginia (the typical customer's own state): gate 0.00 from 0 to 8 calls, +0.50 at 9. The hypothesis omits the West Virginia exception (122 customers), which claim C135's own typical case shows (risk change 0.0). The 'only from 4 calls' wording in blocks[4] and annotations is right (never on below 4). Same omission in hypothesis_revisions.ann_88.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/authoring_v4/drafts_v2/items/dv-e8679c --hold typical --sweep 'number customer service calls=0:9:10' --sweep 'state=West Virginia,Idaho'

findings.statement: More customer-service calls raise the predicted chance ... slowly at first and then faster, and more so in South Dakota.
findings.check: probe calls 0..3 against evening charge 11.76/22.57 and against state South Dakota/West Virginia/Michigan
findings.evidence: The South Dakota effect reproduces (1.0% -> 9.2% vs 1.5% -> 2.9% in West Virginia), but evening charge is the stronger partner and applies to all customers: at 11.76 US dollars the part goes +0.15 -> +2.43 logit (risk 1.1% -> 10.0%); at 22.57 it stays 0 (risk 2.3% flat). The part's title and largest weight (-1.0 per sd) are evening charge, yet no drafted ann_87 sentence names it. South Dakota is 66 customers with test check 'unclear', stated without a hedge. Same in blocks[2] last sentence, annotations.ann_87[2] and hypothesis_revisions.ann_87.

findings.statement: It ignores total daytime charge, total evening calls, total international calls and total night-time charge.
findings.evidence: No path exists (C060 max change 0.0), but C060 itself notes that day charge is tied to day minutes, which the model reads, and asks for 'does not read X itself' rather than 'ignores'.
